newsitem.title: UK: Ford UK unions to vote on holding strike ballot.
newsitem.headline: Ford UK unions to vote on holding strike ballot.

text.p: Union members of Ford Motor Co's British plants will vote over the next week on whether to hold strike action ballots in protest at plans to cut 1,300 jobs at Ford's Halewood plant, the Press Association said on Thursday.

Ford earlier announced job cuts which would reduce the workforce at the Halewood plant near Liverpool in northwest England by one-third and said the new version of the firm's popular Escort model would not be built at the plant.
Ford UK spokesman Tim Collins declined to comment on the unions move to vote on holding a strike ballot.
Britain's Transport and General Workers Union said earlier the job cuts were "morally unacceptable."
Tony Woodley, the union's car industry secretary said union representatives at Ford plants around Britain would "consider a coordinated industrial response" to the planned job losses.

"In placing the entire burden of the cutbacks in its European operations on the backs of the loyal Liverpool workforce, Ford is undoubtedly taking advantage of the couldn't-care-less approach of the present British government," Woodley said.

Although Ford said Halewood could be the site to build a new vehicle, probably a multi-purpose people carrier, it is expected that production of its new Escort model, due in 1999, will now take place at its plants in Spain or Germany.
